headline: Gas, electricity disconnection among 5 penalties for not filing income tax return
summary: Millions of TIN holders in Bangladesh fail to submit income tax returns annually. Non-compliance can lead to severe penalties, including fines, loss of tax benefits, and disconnection of utility services.
details: Around 7.5 million out of 12.5 million Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) holders in Bangladesh do not submit their income tax returns annually. Non-filers with taxable income or those requiring returns for 45 types of services face up to five types of penalties.

Tax officials can impose a fine of 10% of the last assessed tax, with a minimum of BDT 1,000 and a maximum of BDT 50,000, for failing to submit returns on time. An additional BDT 50 per day may be charged if the failure continues, and BDT 50,000 for failing to provide information during an inquiry.

Taxpayers who do not submit returns within the stipulated time will lose their tax exemption benefits. This includes exemptions on investments in government-specified sectors like savings certificates, which would otherwise reduce their tax liability.
Failure to submit returns on time will also incur an additional tax of 2% per month on the imposed tax amount. This penalty applies to the period of delay after the due date.

Tax officials are now empowered to disconnect gas, electricity, and water connections for individuals and industrial units that fail to submit their income tax returns. This applies to any state-provided utility service.

High-grade government and private sector officials are mandated to submit income tax returns. Non-submission can lead to complications in receiving salaries and allowances, as offices often require proof of return submission.

From the current fiscal year, returns can be submitted year-round. While the first three months (July-September) offer tax exemptions, submissions from October to December incur the standard tax. Returns filed from January to June will face both tax and penalties.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman arrives in Tokyo for four-day state visit to deepen Bangladesh-Japan ties
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit, at the invitation of his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi, aims to attract investment, expand trade, and accelerate development cooperation.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived in Tokyo this morning for a four-day official visit, hosted by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The visit is set to deepen bilateral ties, attract investment, and expand trade and development cooperation.

A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight, carrying the prime minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman, and entourage members, landed at Narita International Airport at 9:07am local time. Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Yasutaka Nakasone received the prime minister at the airport.

A motorcade then escorted PM Rahman to Tokyo's Imperial Hotel, where he will reside during his visit. He is scheduled to hold high-level bilateral talks with the Japanese prime minister on October 27, followed by a joint press announcement and a luncheon.

During the visit, the prime minister will also meet Japanese government officials, development institutions, and business leaders. He will visit industrial and energy facilities and deliver the keynote address at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum.

The visit is expected to deepen the existing strategic partnership, attract fresh Japanese investment, and accelerate ongoing development projects. Discussions will focus on the effective implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), signed in February 2026.

The two sides will also explore expanding access for Bangladeshi products to the Japanese market and strengthening business engagement. Wider cooperation in renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, and human resource development is also on the agenda.

PM Rahman's tentative program includes engagements with the Japan-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship League and the chairman of the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation. Meetings are also planned with the presidents of JICA, JBIC, JETRO, and the chairman of the Sasakawa Peace Foundation.

The proposed itinerary includes visits to an LNG terminal and power plant in Futtsu City, Chiba, the headquarters of UNIQLO, and a Toyota factory in Nagoya. Around eight Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and cooperation agreements are under discussion, with three to four expected to be signed.

These agreements cover agriculture, fisheries, human resource development, skills enhancement, civil aviation, trade, environmental conservation, and local government modernisation. Separate agreements are also being pursued in education and human resource development.

Detailed discussions are planned on Japanese support for establishing factories in Bangladesh, generating employment, and developing human resources. The two sides are also expected to discuss regional and international peace and stability, a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis, and stronger cooperation in addressing the energy crisis.

This visit follows the prime minister's participation in an online meeting in April, where Bangladesh welcomed a Japan-led initiative to address energy challenges across Asia. Japan has been a major development partner of Bangladesh since diplomatic relations were established in 1972, supporting key infrastructure projects like the Dhaka metro rail and Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's third terminal.
